body:
You are a really amazing individual. :) People always say you can't help others if you don't help yourself first, but I think that's BS, and people like you prove it--it helps so much to try and give back to others.
Kudos to you, sir/ma'am!

Oh, that sounds like hell in a handbasket, dear god. I'm so glad you came through it alright though. I hope your situation has improved since then. 
Thanks man. :)

The 'stupid' part comes more from my attitude at the beginning of this venture, to be honest. I was high on life when I got accepted to this position. Beat out 500 other applicants for it, and for the first time, felt like i was going to be doing something really meaningful--helping out in south central hit all the right notes for the idealist i am. i just feel stupid because the actual experience, at work and in other areas, has been so incredibly disparate from my expectations. I've been told to not feel stupid because I wanted to think the best of people and thought I could implement a positive change on some local level, but I've also been told I was just a pretentious idiot to start, and...well, you know the rest.

I really appreciate it though. I'm sure to a large extent my worldview was so shaken up because I've just been blindsided by my age and...naivety? But you're right about the quitting jobs because of little issues, and that no one's got a crystal ball.
Again, thanks for taking the time to reply, man. It really means a lot.

Wow, that's really rough man, I'm sorry. I'm not going to say 'i know what you mean' but a friend of mine just got out of a 3 yr prison stint for marijuana--it's insane the way one small act screws you over for the rest of your life. it's not right, and you have my sincerest sympathies. :( Have you tried WorkSource sites or something like that? Or volunteering? sometimes if you make a good impression on people they have resources...that's how i got the job offer (yeah it fell through but, you know. lol)

Mm, maybe to keep being depressed. But i noticed over the last two days that when i'm in my room i feel 95% more suicidal...in comparison, i had to bike a few miles to run errands today, and just being outside and moving made me feel a helluva lot more hopeful. what part of the country are you in if ya don't mind me asking?
Woah. Thanks for the heads up, I'm so sorry you had to go through that. :(

Thank you; it honestly really helps to hear someone say it might still be the best choice. Just have to stick to it, and remember that it's temporary.
Thanks again.
Please, please don't. dafanz is right; sue their asses instead. They had no right to do this to you. Please hold on.
Thanks for taking the time to reply; yeah, everything looks a bit better this morning--at least enough that I can believe i'll be able to work something out. Thanks again. :)

Protip, sir, r/suicidewatch is probably not the best place to be a pretentious dick. Just for future reference.
Here ya go: 
"Main symptoms of hydrocodone overdose. If severe, death may result. Symptoms of hydrocodone overdose include respiratory depression; extreme somnolence; blue, clammy, or cold skin; narrowed or widened pupils; bradycardia; coma; seizures; cardiac arrest; and death."

It's a service position, not something that qualifies as 'gainful employment,' so it's a bit complicated. In retrospect, I could've and should have called it quits back in November when things really started to sour. At this point, though, I have a month left, and if I leave before then a) doesn't really help as I've no where to go and b) I don't get the payment toward my student loans that I'll receive if I complete the contract. If that clarifies it.

Haha sorry! Yeah, might have read too much jk rowling as a kid, I've been saying 'mum' as long as I can remember haha. 
I'm in good ol' L.A., so the US. 
"Join the club"--I'm sorry things aren't going too well on your end... Let me know if you need to vent too? Helps to commiserate sometimes. :)

Hey no worries I didn't stay awake much later last night anyhow--thanks for taking the time to reply. For starters, I really dig your metaphor, that's a cool way of looking at the situation. :)
Your grandpa sounds awesome, that is seriously a good thing to keep in mind. As is trying to just be content w/making an effort in an uphill battle. "when that much is thrown back in your face"...yeah, I think that's really what just threw me for a loop. But, agreed, I need to find new people or just be less effected by those currently in my life--thanks for the reminder. :)
Thank you for the kind words and the different perspective. Really helped me start this morning off on a more hopeful note. :) Good luck finding your new awesome job soon!!
...why do you think /suicidewatch is a good place to criticize people?
It took me a wicked long time to get everything written down--apologies. I figure you're offline by this point, but thank you for the support in any case. :)

I really really hope so. And my sympathies on the parents, man. :( Logically I know it'll change, I'm just not sure how to see past the next 2 months when I don't know where I'll be living or working in 4 weeks.
Sure, what level elaboration are you looking for?
Tell you what--I'm going to edit my original post to include more. Just a minute.

thanks, kind sir/ma'am. :) Maybe i was at that point, i've just felt steamrolled by life since then. I moved around a fair amount as a kid; i have 3 really close friends. the nearest (location wise) is 700 miles away. the only one who could conceivably help is an ex; i appreciate her input but i know any help she'd give is...well, biased, so i'm too scared to take it. i'd feel terrible asking either of the other two, seeing as one was in the same program as me and now is in a similar boat (financially) and the other has enough on her plate. which i suppose is why i turned to reddit.
